properties.bedrock_type: Gullane Formation Sandstone and Igneous Basalt intrusions
properties.mineralogy: Quartz-rich carboniferous sedimentary sandstone with volcanic basalt outcroppings
properties.drainage: Steep valley-side hydraulic descent into the incised Water of Leith riverbed

properties.primary_surfacing: Traditional Scottish granite sett cobblestones, flagstone pavements, and riverside retaining walls
properties.wear_characteristics: Moisture-darkened drainage gutters, damp biological patina, smoothed stone wear along vehicular courtyards
properties.micro_grading: Terraced gorge topography descending rapidly from Rothesay Terrace plateau down into Dean Village hollow

properties.groundcover: Dense deciduous river-gorge woodland canopy, riparian mosses, and clinging wall vegetation

properties.primary_building_typology: Scots Baronial and 19th-century vernacular milling village housing

structures.name: Well Court (Central Baronial Complex)
structures.roof_geometry: Steeply pitched red clay pantile and Scottish slate roofs with crow-stepped gables, conical-roofed corner turrets (tourelles), and a central polygonal clock tower with lead spire
structures.facade_material: Course-squared red/buff sandstone ashlar and rubble masonry
structures.weathering_patina: Deep atmospheric soot and carbon encrustation in cornice reveals, carved stone strapwork, and rain-washed upper ashlar

structures.name: Hawthornbank Lane / Dean Path Terraces (Flanking Tenements)
structures.roof_geometry: Pitched Scottish slate and red pantile dormered roofs with heavy stone chimney stacks
structures.facade_material: Harled/rendered pale sandstone rubble and exposed dressed stone dressings
structures.weathering_patina: Mineral wash lines, wet mortar repointing, and localized soot accumulation beneath sills

structures.name: Background Terraces (Bells Mills / Rothesay Plunge Enclosure)
structures.roof_geometry: Continuous pitched slate rooflines with multiple gabled wall-head dormers
structures.facade_material: Pale lime-harled masonry with exposed sandstone quoins
structures.weathering_patina: Even graying and rain streak patina along northern exposure

period_vehicles: Parked modern European estate cars and hatchbacks in court cul-de-sac
pedestrian_profiles: Occasional local residents and walkers on the Water of Leith Walkway

properties.lighting_condition: Crisp temperate midday Scottish sunlight with soft atmospheric dispersion and defined, raking shadows across valley slopes
